title: Canonical divisorial log-etale map from a rank-one Kummer presentation
statement: Let A and B be strictly henselian discrete valuation domains [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], in one scheme universe, with an injective algebra map A -> B. Let n>0 be a unit of A, pi a uniformizer of A and tau a uniformizer of B, with tau^n=pi. Suppose evaluation at tau gives an A-algebra equivalence A[X]/(X^n-pi) -> B [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. Then there are locally Noetherian fs log schemes SB and T [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], isomorphisms of their schemes to Spec B and Spec A, and a log morphism q:SB -> T. Their log monoid sheaves, over their structural maps, are isomorphic to the canonical divisorial log presheaves for Spec Frac B -> Spec B and Spec Frac A -> Spec A. The underlying q is exactly Spec(A -> B) under the specified isomorphisms, and q is log etale [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale]. This statement makes no group-action, completeness or mixed-characteristic assumption.

source.place: ILO VI 2.1-2.2, pp.71-72, standard Kummer etale covers; XVI 3.7, p.254; step 8 of lem-per-tame-trait-quotient-log-etale

proof.text: On Spec C, for C=A,B, use the divisorial presheaf for the actual generic-point inclusion. A section is a regular function whose pullback to the generic fibre is invertible. These form a sheaf: regular functions glue uniquely along etale covers, and invertibility is etale local and hence descends. The structural map is the actual inclusion in the multiplicative structure sheaf; its preimage over the units is exactly the sheaf of units. Pullback along the injective map A -> B preserves these sections, since it gives the compatible generic-field map. Thus it supplies the canonical log morphism over the spectrum map. The following chart computation proves the structures are fs and the morphism is log etale.

source.place: Expose VI 2.1--2.2, printed pp.71--72; rank-one Kummer chart calculated explicitly.

proof.text: A uniformizer $a$ of either strictly henselian DVR $C=A,B$ gives the chart $\mathbf N\to C$, $1\mapsto a$, for its canonical divisorial log structure. Indeed at the closed geometric point the sections-to-stalk bijection [lem-weil-pbc-sets-strictly-henselian-open-sections-stalk] identifies that log monoid with $C\setminus\{0\}$; every such element is uniquely $a^r c$ with $r\geq0$, $c\in C^\times$. At the generic point $a$ is a unit and both log structures are trivial. These verify exactly the logification stalk test of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]; $\mathbf N$ is fine and saturated. With $a=\pi,\tau$, the assumed uniformizer equation gives a compatible chart $\mathbf N\xrightarrow{\times n}\mathbf N$ for $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$. Its group map has zero kernel and cokernel $\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$ of invertible order. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], the comparison target has coordinate ring $A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[z]}\mathbf Z[x]=A[x]/(x^n-\pi)$, where $z\mapsto\pi$ and $z\mapsto x^n$; this tensor identity follows by sending $x$ to its class and the inverse map by the two structure homomorphisms. The comparison is the assumed evaluation isomorphism. An isomorphism is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], so the chart definition [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale] proves log etaleness.

theorem trait_kummer_divisorial_logEtale
    (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [IsDomain A] [IsDomain B]
    [IsDiscreteValuationRing A] [IsDiscreteValuationRing B]
    [IsStrictlyHenselianLocalRing A] [IsStrictlyHenselianLocalRing B]
    [Algebra A B] (hinj : Function.Injective (algebraMap A B))
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (hunit : IsUnit (n : A))
    (pi : A) (hpi : Irreducible pi) (tau : B) (htau : Irreducible tau)
    (hpow : tau ^ n = algebraMap A B pi)
    (e : (A[X] ⧸ Ideal.span {X ^ n - C pi}) ≃ₐ[A] B)
    (he : ∀ Q : A[X], e (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ Q) = aeval tau Q) :
    ∃ (SB T : FineSaturatedLogScheme.{u})
      (eB : SB.scheme ≅ Spec (.of B))
      (eT : T.scheme ≅ Spec (.of A))
      (q : EtaleLogHom SB T),
      (∃ e : SB.logStructure.monoidSheaf.obj ≅ divisorialLogPresheaf
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap B (FractionRing B))) ≫ eB.inv),
        e.hom ≫ divisorialStructuralMap
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap B (FractionRing B))) ≫ eB.inv) =
            SB.logStructure.alpha) ∧
      (∃ e : T.logStructure.monoidSheaf.obj ≅ divisorialLogPresheaf
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A
            (FractionRing A))) ≫ eT.inv),
        e.hom ≫ divisorialStructuralMap
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A
            (FractionRing A))) ≫ eT.inv) =
              T.logStructure.alpha) ∧
      q.base ≫ eT.hom = eB.hom ≫
        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A B)) ∧
      q.IsLogEtale
